speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: There have been several positive developments in the recent months both in philanthropy and also in Government initiatives to support the more financially vulnerable in our society.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: These come at a crucial time of need for several in our midst.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Here, we have a generous Government providing the option for those who are in a position to in turn generously share with charitable causes.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Besides the gift of the money itself, I am sure that this will also raise awareness of needs and causes in our midst.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: In recent years, we have also heard these words repeated by our national leaders: "No one gets left behind".

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: I do hope that this will find its way to be a shared national aspiration alongside our Government's commitment.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: What do our Parliament records show about the word "generosity" or "generous"?

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Well, as I prepared for this paper, I did a simple word search on our Parliament website.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: For the word "generosity", there were nine results and for the word "generous", there were 38 results.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: I then searched the word "money" and there were 1,790 results.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: And I looked at the next word, "finance" and it displayed 3,680 results.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Our fellow citizens and residents came out in so many different ways to help one another.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: We did not need a committee or extensive discussions or we did not need to fill out multiple pages of applications.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Many across all strata of our society stepped forward in small and not so small ways.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Public, private and people sectors acted spontaneously, responding to needs from basic necessities to financial support and financial support for both individuals as well as businesses and to caring for each other.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: So, this does beg the question: can we be a continuously generous and caring society now that we have settled in the post-pandemic new norm?

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: I do believe we can if we want to and work towards a shared vision of our future; and I would say, much along the aspirations shared by way of feedback through Forward Singapore.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Tertiary institution research carried out in recent years on philanthropy in Singapore show that generosity is a visible though often silent thread that flows through our heritage and history.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: At many stages in our modern history since 1819, the whole of society have stepped forward.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Our earliest philanthropists were individuals and families from across the main racial groups.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: I hope that there will be opportunity to make the history of Singapore philanthropy and generosity more available and accessible.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: In the simplest definition, this describes the active engagement and mobilising of all of society in acts of giving and generosity.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: These would be through giving of time such as volunteerism and befriending, the giving of talent such as giving expertise and programme development and also the giving of treasures through direct donations.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Grassroots philanthropy continues to grow and thrive in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: The good work of groups such as the National Volunteer and Philanthropy Centre (NVPC) and National Council of Social Service (NCSS) is encouraging the growth of all three areas of generous giving.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: If I look back, the response that we see in appeals for help and contributions should continue to be an encouragement to all of us.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: I recall years back, how society responded in highly generous giving when we became aware of, for example, a foreign worker injured and needing financial help or individuals and their families needing particular financial support for specialised medical treatments.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: To achieve this we will need to be intentional.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: We can cover this at the earliest stages starting in our schools, progressing it through our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs).

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: We can encourage this through youth programmes and organisations.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: We can bring this deeper through existing initiatives such a NVPC's City of Good and Companies of Good.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: We can encourage families to give as a family across all generations.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: We will certainly benefit from engaging our seniors in acts and activities around generosity.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Religion plays a key role in shaping generosity by the very nature of the teaching of kindness, respect, love and compassion.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: The majority of Singaporeans belong to one of the major religious groups.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Our mosques, temples, churches and other places of worship all contribute toward a culture of generosity in multiracial and multi-religious Singapore.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: The support of our religious leaders will definitely strengthen our collective efforts and collective responsibility.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: These are just some example of ways that we can build on an existing generous society.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: The values we have been teaching and inculcating have already contributed toward a more caring and compassionate society – and I do hope we keep building on this.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: One on the $2.50 shop which is keeping food affordable for needy customers.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Ms Hani and her family are a wonderful example of one of many forms of grassroots philanthropy.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Let us remember that as a fledgling independent nation we benefited from the generosity of larger and more developed nations.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: We also benefited from the generosity of our local philanthropic community such as the early foundations established by successful families.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Education and training overseas was an important area where we were able to build up a key team for our public sector and essential services.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Colombo Plan scholarships are one example of the generosity of others during our crucial early years.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Some of our early scholars became political leaders.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Our professionals have also benefited from acquiring knowledge, skills and expertise to improve many aspects of our society in areas such as medicine and healthcare.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Gradually, with the transfer of knowledge and our own economic growth, we began to build up our own capabilities.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: In recent decades we are now sharing this through ASEAN scholarships, and also inviting public sector leaders from the region to attend the Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy, just to cite a couple of examples.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: The establishment of Temasek Foundation and Singapore International Foundation (SIF) are also tangible initiatives that help to benefit and serve communities outside of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: I believe our foreign missions can also increasingly serve as a conduit of generosity for us as a nation.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: While there are the natural and the normal priorities for our foreign missions such as economic and trade development, diplomacy and political engagement, we can also, through our foreign missions, continue to plant seeds of generosity in tangible and meaningful ways.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: I visited Myanmar in the aftermath of Cyclone Nargis and had several meetings with our then Ambassador.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: He was personally engaged in helping local communities in development initiatives, among which, would be the provision of affordable, clean water solutions.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Our Non-Resident Ambassadors can be bearers of generosity to countries where we find ourselves in a position to offer help.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: As a nation, we also regularly respond to appeals, unfortunately accompanying natural disasters, and we respond with donations in kind and at times with medical and humanitarian aid.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: During COVID-19, we also helped countries around us to tackle the pandemic and our neighbours have acknowledged this, with appreciation.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: The more recent introduction of tax offsetting for approved foreign charitable donations is another step toward enhancing our place as a generous nation.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: The ranking covers categories such as "would you willing to help a stranger", "donating money" and "volunteering".

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: At the top of the list, Indonesia, has topped the global ranking under this report for six years.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: It may be of interest to note that the SIF's annual Young Social Entrepreneurs programme, attracts a high level of interest from Indonesian participants.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: A nation with a spirit of generosity is a breath of fresh air to a troubled world.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Allow me to summarise and conclude with some thoughts and suggestions for further consideration.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: A visionary Singapore philanthropist shared this idea recently.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: The more I reflect on it, the more strongly I feel we should take this suggestion seriously as we continue to develop Singapore as a philanthropy hub.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Thirdly, as I touched on briefly earlier, promote giving as a family.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: We can action this as part of bringing generosity to the next level and to encourage active participation across all generations.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: My generation may be more comfortable with direct donations and this is still one of the more common methods.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Amongst the younger generation, there may be more interest in volunteerism and direct engagement.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Fourthly, encourage and nurture Singaporeans to become ambassadors for good.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: We have one of the most accessible passports in the world.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Yes, this enables us to pursue our business and economic interests, and there is great benefit for that.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Yes, this also makes our leisure pursuits more convenient.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: But how about actively considering the social opportunity that this presents?

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: We are seeing this, over the years, growing very much so locally.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: I would propose to encourage that we encourage stronger and intentional public, private and people sector collaboration.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Temasek Foundation and SIF, our larger private foundations and philanthropic groups can increasingly take the lead to bring generosity beyond our borders as Team Singapore.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: I am thinking of an approach similar to the Enterprise Singapore support for local companies to internationalise.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: We need to maintain a healthy balance between donor and beneficiary organisation.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Beneficiary organisations are expected to be responsible and accountable for public funds and donations.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Donors may need to recognise and appreciate that the beneficiary organisations are expected to deliver high levels of service in their area of specialisation.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: They may also be more attuned to needs on the ground and therefore more knowledgeable, both in service delivery and needs.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: While fiduciary responsibility remains a collective responsibility, not every aspect of service delivery can be brought back to a simple cost denominator.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Eight, maybe we need to rethink the phrase "he who pays the piper calls the tune".

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: We need to provide adequate space so that there is regular and adequate input from service providers and their beneficiaries.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Ninth, we have had an extensive discussion on this, harness technology.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Technology has been playing an increasingly key role in the non-profit sector.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Let us continue to harness technology for all appropriate purposes and specifically for doing good.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: The aspirations of our people are for a more caring, compassionate and generous society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: His vision for Singapore echoes the aspirations many Singaporeans shared during our Forward Singapore engagement last year – to live in a society that is fair, inclusive and united, where we look out for others and support those in need.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: All of us experienced that firsthand during the COVID-19 pandemic, when people from all walks of life volunteered, donated, cared, making a difference to our community, our society and our nation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chua spoke about grassroots philanthropy and mobilising the whole of society in acts of giving and generosity beyond the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) is striving to make this vision a reality by creating more avenues for everyone to contribute in their own unique ways.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: One avenue to do this is through our SG Cares Volunteer Centres.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We have set up SG Cares Volunteer Centres in 24 towns to connect residents, businesses, schools and other stakeholders with local volunteering opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These Volunteer Centres work with Government agencies and community partners on the ground to identify and address pressing needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For example, Volunteer Centres work with Active Ageing Centres to engage our seniors and help keep them physically active as well as socially connected.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, please join one of the 24 Volunteer Centres around Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chua also spoke about encouraging people at different stages of life to give back to society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We believe that giving as a habit can start as early as when our children are in preschool.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Therefore, we have programmes in place to do just that.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA)'s "Start Small Dream Big" initiative and our Values in Action experiences in Ministry of Education (MOE) schools aim to inculcate empathy and a spirit of giving among our children and students.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our SG Cares office also works with the National University of Singapore to integrate service learning into their curriculum through a credit-bearing course that gets students to volunteer with seniors in our communities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And as our students enter the workforce and they already get a taste of what it is like to volunteer as students, we hope they will continue to do so as they start working.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To foster this spirit, MCCY partners professional associations from the legal, medical, accounting and engineering sectors to encourage professionals to volunteer their skills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For example, the Law Society's Pro Bono SG partners universities to inculcate a habit of volunteering among law students by encouraging the students complete 20 pro bono hours and channelling them to intern at its community law centre.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Once they have graduated, Pro Bono SG continues to provide volunteer lawyers with avenues to volunteer and serve the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Beyond school and work, MCCY is also working with NVPC to rally businesses to give back to society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Businesses who are keen to do more can join NVPC's Company of Good programme, which helps businesses give back through corporate giving or by redesigning their business practices to benefit society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As advisor to the Company of Good Roundtable, I encourage businesses to join the Company of Good, because they do plenty of good.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chua also suggested that Singapore could become a Silicon Valley for philanthropy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are establishing Singapore as a regional philanthropy hub and making it easier for people and businesses to give.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: There is much more we can do and indeed plan to do, but let me share what we have been doing collectively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The Wealth Management Institute and the Private Banking Industry Group launched the Impact Philanthropy Partnership (IPP) last year, with support from the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS).

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: IPP helps work with high networth individuals and families to support philanthropic activities and causes, to foster partnerships and to drive impactful giving.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Temasek Trust, which Mr Chua mentioned, also launched the Philanthropy Asia Alliance (PAA) last year, gathering philanthropists, governments and businesses to develop novel solutions for social and environmental challenges in our region.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This includes advancing education for girls in India and enabling healthcare access in the Philippines.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are also deploying finance, including philanthropic capital, to address the world's pressing challenges like climate change.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MAS also launched the Philanthropy Tax Incentive Scheme (PTIS) last year to encourage overseas giving among Single Family Offices in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: PTIS approved qualifying donors can claim tax deductions on overseas donations that are channelled through qualifying local intermediaries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We also regularly review our policies and programmes to support local giving.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Apart from tax incentives, we also work with partners like The Majurity Trust (TMT) and Community Foundation of Singapore (CFS) to drive impactful giving.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: TMT works with philanthropists, companies and other stakeholders to foster collaboration within the philanthropic ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It supports ground-up groups and non-profit organisations to address community issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I work closely with the team at TMT and attended their Majurity Night last month, where over 200 of Singapore's leading philanthropists, corporates and nonprofit charities gathered to channel their giving and expertise to the many worthy causes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As Mr Chua recalled, our early pioneer philanthropists built Singapore through their generous giving.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our early pioneer philanthropists worked with the community and local groups to build the Singapore that we see today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Today, in modern, thriving Singapore, we have even more resources, more causes to impact and more ways to connect both to facilitate and to catalyse giving.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Heed Mr Chua's call to action to partner us to bring our shared vision to life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: If you are a business, please join NVPC's Company of Good or check out the work that organisations like TMT are doing on the ground.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, let us not only speak more about generosity in Parliament and in Singapore, but also act in generosity, because as Winston Churchill said famously, "We make a living by what we get, but we make a life by what we give."       Adjourned accordingly at 8.25 pm.
